P9_live_feed_detector.source: Iowa State HADS live-feed copy, 125 big-rise or labelled gauges in the 7 pilot floods (121 with live data), pulled 17 Nov 2026; data/live_detector_pilot.csv; rules in code/gd_live_rules.py
P9_live_feed_detector.silence_rule: gap of at least max(3 x usual interval, 60 min) right after a 0.5 ft rise in the previous hour; the alarm fires when the gap reaches that length. Caught 9 of 12 SILENT gauges and 5 of 7 live-only outages; fired at 1 of 81 other archive-healthy gauges. With a 15-min floor instead of 60: 10 of 12, 6 of 7, still 1 of 81.
P9_live_feed_detector.implausible_rule: caught 6 of 6 IMPLAUSIBLE gauges; scoring uses the archive crest only after the fact
P9_live_feed_detector.impossible_values_beyond_the_dark_set: 20 of 121 gauges sent at least one impossible value (negative, above the true crest, error code 1310.71, or a drop to 0 that reverts); 12 of them have a clean archive, so the error was removed later and is invisible to archive studies. 15 of the 20 are Harvey (2017).
P9_live_feed_detector.op_max_false_alarms: 7 gauges where the real crest rose above the published operational maximum (e.g. 03466500: crest 66.03 ft, limit 60 ft), so op max alone is not a safe ceiling
P9_live_feed_detector.frozen_rule: flat within 0.1 ft for 2 h, 3 ft above pre-event level, after a 1 ft rise: caught 4 of 8 FROZEN but fired at 24 of 81 archive-healthy gauges (broad natural crests are also flat). A single-gauge frozen rule is not usable; needs a neighbour check.
P9_live_feed_detector.under_read: 0 of 2 caught by single-gauge rules; needs the neighbour rule
P9_live_feed_detector.caveat: In-sample: rules designed after seeing these floods. Labels are mine (P3), not yet hand-checked by the student.
P9_live_feed_detector.hunt_timing: Hunt sent readings every 5 min until 29.45 ft at 09:35 UTC (4:35 am CDT). The Iowa State copy also holds the later-inserted crest 37.52 ft at 10:10 UTC, which was ignored. With the 60-min floor the real-time alarm fires at 10:35 UTC, after the USGS-estimated crest time; with a 15-min floor it fires at 09:50 UTC (4:50 am CDT), 20 min before it. The floor matters for flash floods.
